newsitem.title: USA: Calif. tax measure could lead to downgrades - Nuveen.
newsitem.headline: Calif. tax measure could lead to downgrades - Nuveen.

text.p: A controversial California tax measure approved by voters earlier this month will likely result in rating downgrades for some local governments, according to a John Nuveen & Co Inc report.

Proposition 218, approved by voters on Nov. 5, strengthens existing law to require that local taxes be submitted to voters for approval. It also allows property owners to approve assessments and strictly limits the use of fees and charges.
"While we do not, at this time, anticipate bond defaults as a result of Proposition 218, we believe that downgrades are likely," the John Nuveen report concluded.
"Proposition 218 is quite clearly a credit negative for California's local government issuers," the report said.
John Nuveen's report said the complex measure would likely lead to a series of legal battles which will ultimately determine the parameters for its interpretation.
Proposition 218 has drawn fire from local government officials in California and municipal analysts across the country.
The Los Angeles City Council decided last week to sue over the California measure.
Los Angeles could be the first local government to go to court over the measure, but it was not expected to be the last local government to sue in the months ahead.
Moody's Investors Service Inc has warned that the credit ratings of some local governments in the state could be undermined by a controversial tax measure.

The John Nuveen report said Proposition 218 should have no impact on the state's creditworthiness. Redevelopment agency tax allocation bonds issued before the Nov. 5 election should also not be affected, Nuveen said.
Nuveen said Mello-Roos bonds and most water and sewer revenue bonds should not be hurt.
"We do, however, express a general concern about the use of maintenance and other assessments as revenues," it said.
Nuveen said leases would likely be the most severly impacted of all obligations, as they are secured only from available general fund revenues.
